articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Vaccine Stimulates Immune Response in 90 Percent of High-Risk Patients in Early Trial
articles.excerpt: An off-the-shelf vaccine targeting KRAS mutations showed durable T-cell responses and no cancer recurrence after 16.5 months of follow-up, raising hopes for one of the deadliest cancers.
articles.image_caption: A medical researcher examines samples in a laboratory. Experimental vaccines targeting KRAS gene mutations have shown promising results in early pancreatic cancer trials.
articles.nri_angle: Pancreatic cancer is the third leading cause of cancer death in the US, and the breakthrough offers hope for early-detection strategies and preventive treatment relevant to health-conscious diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: California Makes Diwali an Official Statewide Holiday, Joining Pennsylvania and Connecticut
articles.excerpt: The law signed by Governor Newsom allows state employees to take paid leave and public schools to close on the Festival of Lights, starting in 2026.
articles.image_caption: Diwali celebrations with traditional diyas and lights. California has become the third US state to designate the Festival of Lights as an official statewide holiday, recognizing its nearly one million Indian Americans.
articles.nri_angle: California is home to nearly 960,000 Indian Americans — the largest such population in any US state — who now have official recognition for their most widely celebrated festival.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Skyrocketing School Fees Are Squeezing Indian Families as Education Inflation Outpaces Income Growth
articles.excerpt: With private school costs rising 10 to 12 percent annually and coaching expenses nearly matching tuition by secondary school, Indian families are caught between aspiration and affordability.
articles.image_caption: Indian schoolgirls in uniform attend class at a private school. Rising fees and ancillary costs are putting quality education out of reach for many middle-class families.
articles.nri_angle: NRI families face the same cost squeeze whether educating children in India or abroad, with coaching expenses and fee hikes eroding household budgets across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: West Nile Virus Hits 22-Year High in the US as Oregon Reports First 2026 Case
articles.excerpt: The CDC has confirmed cases across 23 states, with Arizona accounting for the most infections and four deaths — nearly five times the historical average for this point in the season.
articles.image_caption: A woman applies insect repellent before going outdoors. The CDC has urged Americans to take precautions against mosquito bites as West Nile virus cases reach a 22-year high.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families across the US, particularly in warm-climate states with large NRI populations, face heightened exposure risk during outdoor summer activities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Common Antibiotics Are Failing: The Global Resistance Crisis Explained
articles.excerpt: One in six bacterial infections worldwide now resists treatment, and India — where over-the-counter antibiotic sales remain rampant — faces among the highest resistance rates on the planet.
articles.image_caption: Assorted antibiotic pills and capsules displayed at a pharmacy. Antibiotic resistance is rising globally, with the WHO warning that one in six bacterial infections now resists treatment.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora members should be aware of high AMR rates in India when travelling, and avoid over-the-counter antibiotic purchases that fuel resistance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Losing Just 80 Minutes of Sleep a Night Leads to Weight Gain, Columbia Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A six-week randomised trial shows that even mild, chronic sleep restriction caused participants to gain weight and become significantly more sedentary — a pattern that affects nearly a third of adults worldwide.
articles.image_caption: A woman sleeps on a pillow. A Columbia University study found that cutting sleep by just 80 minutes a night for six weeks led to measurable weight gain and increased sedentary behaviour.
articles.nri_angle: With 46 percent of Indian adults sleeping less than six hours a night and India ranked among the most sleep-deprived nations globally, the study's findings on weight gain from mild sleep loss carry outsized relevance for the Indian diaspora juggling long work hours across time zones.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Alzheimer's Blood Test Can Predict Dementia Risk Five to Ten Years Before Symptoms Appear
articles.excerpt: A major study across six international cohorts found that elevated p-tau217 levels in cognitively healthy adults signal future cognitive decline, bringing presymptomatic screening closer to reality.
articles.image_caption: An elderly woman experiencing cognitive distress. A new blood test measuring p-tau217 levels can predict Alzheimer's risk years before symptoms emerge.
articles.nri_angle: Growing elderly Indian American population faces rising Alzheimer's prevalence, and a non-invasive blood test could enable earlier intervention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Blood Test Detects 90% of Early-Stage Pancreatic Cancers, Japanese Study Finds
articles.excerpt: Researchers at Kanazawa University developed a whole-blood gene expression test that outperformed existing markers in catching the deadliest common cancer at its most treatable stage.
articles.image_caption: A blood vacutainer and slide prepared for laboratory testing. A new mRNA-based blood test can detect 90% of early-stage pancreatic cancers, offering hope for earlier diagnosis.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians have elevated diabetes rates, a key pancreatic cancer risk factor, making early detection advances directly relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Serum Institute to Manufacture World's First New TB Vaccine in a Century
articles.excerpt: India's largest vaccine maker partners with Gates Medical Research Institute to produce M72/AS01E, investing over $100 million to prepare for potential approval of a shot that could prevent 76 million new TB cases globally.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional administers a vaccine injection. Serum Institute of India will manufacture the M72/AS01E tuberculosis vaccine candidate under a new agreement with the Gates Medical Research Institute.
articles.nri_angle: Serum Institute's role in manufacturing a potential breakthrough TB vaccine highlights India's central position in global public health and its fight against the country's highest-burden infectious disease.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric's Health Benefits: What Science Says About the Golden Spice
articles.excerpt: From easing joint pain to supporting heart health and memory, clinical research is validating what Ayurvedic practitioners have known for centuries about curcumin's anti-inflammatory power.
articles.image_caption: Ground turmeric powder and fresh turmeric root on a wooden surface. Clinical studies are validating the anti-inflammatory and pain-relief properties of curcumin, the golden spice's active compound.
articles.nri_angle: Turmeric has been central to Indian cooking and Ayurvedic medicine for millennia; Western clinical research is now confirming health benefits long practiced in Indian households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How Chronic Stress Quietly Drives Up Blood Sugar and Diabetes Risk
articles.excerpt: New research shows daily stress causes measurable glucose spikes in insulin-resistant individuals, reinforcing the case for stress management as a frontline diabetes prevention strategy.
articles.image_caption: A person uses a lancet pen and glucometer to test blood sugar levels. New research links chronic stress to measurable glucose spikes in insulin-resistant individuals.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians carry genetic predispositions that make them more vulnerable to stress-related glucose dysregulation, with India's 89.8 million diabetics and 43% undiagnosed rate making this a deeply personal issue for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Archana Puran Singh Adopts Strict Ayurvedic Routine After 15-Day Bengaluru Retreat
articles.excerpt: The 63-year-old actor and Kapil Show regular has cut sugar, maida, and fried food from her diet, now eats dinner at 7 PM and sleeps by 10 PM after completing an Ayurvedic wellness programme.
articles.image_caption: Archana Puran Singh at a public event in 2024. The veteran actor recently completed a 15-day Ayurvedic wellness retreat in Bengaluru.
articles.nri_angle: Ayurvedic wellness retreats in India are attracting rising interest from NRIs reconnecting with traditional health practices, with centres in Karnataka, Kerala, and Goa reporting increased bookings from overseas visitors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dementia Risk Factors Vary Sharply Across Countries, Lancet Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A new analysis of 214,000 older adults across 14 countries reveals that while the risk factors for dementia differ dramatically by region, they cluster in strikingly similar patterns worldwide.
articles.image_caption: A doctor holds an elderly patient's hands during a consultation. A new cross-national study finds that dementia risk factors like education, obesity, and hypertension vary sharply across 14 countries.
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants may carry distinct lifetime risk profiles shaped by conditions in India, where low education and vision loss dominate dementia risk, rather than the obesity and social isolation patterns common in Western countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ankita Konwar Becomes First Assamese Woman to Cross the English Channel, Learned to Swim Just Three Years Ago
articles.excerpt: The endurance athlete and wife of fitness icon Milind Soman completed the iconic Dover-to-Calais crossing as part of an international relay team, marking the 100th anniversary of the first woman's Channel swim.
articles.image_caption: An open-water swimmer cuts through the waves wearing a bright swim cap. Ankita Konwar completed the English Channel relay crossing on July 3, becoming the first woman from Northeast India to achieve the feat.
articles.nri_angle: Konwar's journey from non-swimmer to Channel crosser in three years celebrates extraordinary Indian achievement and Northeast Indian representation on the global stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Summer Sunshine Alone Won't Fix Vitamin D Deficiency — Especially for South Asians
articles.excerpt: A new UK study finds vitamin D levels barely improve even in summer for older adults and people with darker skin. For Indians — at home and in the diaspora — the problem runs deeper than a lack of sunlight.
articles.image_caption: Sunlight streaming through a natural setting. A new study finds that summer sunshine alone is insufficient to correct vitamin D deficiency for older adults and people with darker skin.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face compounding risk factors for vitamin D deficiency — darker skin pigmentation, northern-latitude living and vegetarian diets — making year-round supplementation essential.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclospora Parasite Outbreak Sickens Thousands Across the US With Taco Bell Lettuce Under Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: More than 5,100 possible cases of cyclosporiasis have been reported across 30 states, with shredded iceberg lettuce from a Mexican supplier linked to infections at Taco Bell.
articles.image_caption: Fresh lettuce leaves displayed at a grocery store. Federal investigators have linked shredded iceberg lettuce from a Mexican facility to a cyclosporiasis outbreak affecting more than 5,100 people across the United States.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects Indians living in the US who eat at chain restaurants and buy produce from major grocery stores.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala's Monsoon Flu Crisis: 4,405 Influenza Cases and 49 Deaths in 2026
articles.excerpt: Kerala is grappling with a severe influenza outbreak driven by H1N1 and other strains as monsoon season intensifies, with the state recording the highest flu-related fatalities among all communicable diseases this year.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare worker prepares medical supplies at a clinic. Kerala's public health infrastructure has been mobilized across all districts to manage the influenza surge during the 2026 monsoon season.
articles.nri_angle: The outbreak poses a direct concern for the large Keralite diaspora, many of whom travel home during the monsoon season. Health experts advise travelers to India's southern states to get vaccinated before visiting and take standard respiratory precautions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ozempic and Cancer: Why the Promising Headlines Outpace the Science
articles.excerpt: More than two dozen studies presented at a major oncology conference suggest GLP-1 drugs may reduce cancer risk, but researchers warn the evidence is observational and clinical trials are still needed.
articles.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy. Researchers are investigating whether GLP-1 drugs may have anti-cancer properties beyond their established metabolic benefits.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian communities face elevated diabetes and metabolic syndrome rates, making GLP-1 drug findings on cancer risk especially relevant for India and the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Approves Wegovy for Fatty Liver Disease in New Milestone for GLP-1 Drugs
articles.excerpt: India's drug regulator has cleared Novo Nordisk's semaglutide injection for treating MASH, a serious form of fatty liver disease that affects roughly two in three Indians, making it the first GLP-1 drug approved for this condition both globally and in India.
articles.image_caption: A medical professional prepares a syringe for injection. Wegovy is administered as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection using a prefilled pen device.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians are disproportionately susceptible to metabolic liver disease, and the approval gives family in India access to a treatment previously limited to Western markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DRC Ebola Cases Exceed 2,000 Amid Health Worker Strikes
articles.excerpt: Strikes disrupt critical response efforts as the outbreak escalates in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.image_caption: Health workers in protective equipment during an Ebola response operation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The ongoing Ebola outbreak and health worker strikes in the DRC could impact travel and health security for the Indian diaspora with connections to the region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Cup of Dahi and a 30-Minute Walk May Slow Aging at the Cellular Level, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A clinical trial published in Aging showed that yogurt, moderate exercise, and dietary tweaks reduced the pace of biological aging by 2.2% in just 12 weeks — independent of weight loss.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of yogurt — consuming 100 grams daily was part of the anti-aging intervention studied by researchers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Dahi (plain yogurt) has been a daily staple in Indian households for generations — this clinical trial validates that the tradition may carry real anti-aging benefits at the cellular level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Structured Lifestyle Changes Improved Brain Health by 55% in At-Risk Adults, Landmark AAIC Study Shows
articles.excerpt: The LatAm-FINGERS trial, presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference 2026 in London and published in The Lancet, found that coached exercise, adapted diets, cognitive training, and social engagement dramatically boosted memory and thinking in older adults across 11 countries.
articles.image_caption: An fMRI brain scan — a landmark AAIC study found structured lifestyle changes improved cognitive function by 55% in at-risk adults (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated dementia risk factors by midlife. This landmark trial shows that the coached lifestyle changes most effective for brain health — group exercise, adapted diets, social engagement — mirror traditions already embedded in diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three Asian Americans With Serious Distress Goes Untreated, Largest NYC Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A population-based study of 6,648 Asian American adults in New York City found that stigma, cost, and a lack of culturally matched therapists are leaving a fast-growing community without the mental health care it needs.
articles.image_caption: Insight Therapy Solutions
articles.nri_angle: The cultural barriers to mental health care identified in this NYC study — stigma, self-reliance, lack of matched therapists — are replicated across South Asian communities in the US, Canada, and UK, compounding the diaspora's already elevated cardiovascular risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Cut Dementia Risk by 29% — and Your Dadi's Kitchen Had It Right All Along
articles.excerpt: A landmark 15-year study in JAMA Network Open found that diets rich in vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of traditional South Asian cooking — significantly lower the odds of cognitive decline, even in people already showing early signs of Alzheimer's.
articles.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, legumes, and whole grains — staples of anti-inflammatory eating patterns linked to lower dementia risk
articles.nri_angle: Traditional South Asian diets rich in anti-inflammatory ingredients like turmeric, dal, and whole grains align closely with the eating pattern shown to cut dementia risk — a critical finding for a community at elevated cardiometabolic risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Weeks of Walking With Poles Cut Depression Symptoms in Half, a Landmark Trial Found
articles.excerpt: A randomized controlled trial published in the Journal of Affective Disorders found that supervised Nordic walking led to clinical remission in up to 53% of participants — offering a low-cost, stigma-free path to mental health care that could resonate in South Asian communities.
articles.image_caption: Nordic walking engages up to 90 percent of the body's muscles, turning a simple walk into a full-body workout
articles.nri_angle: Community walking groups are already a fixture in South Asian diaspora neighborhoods — this study suggests adding structure to what people already do could yield clinical-grade mental health benefits in a culturally comfortable, stigma-free way.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 14 Indian Cities Rank Among the World's Most Heat-Vulnerable. Here's What That Means for Your Family Back Home.
articles.excerpt: A new Oxford University analysis of cities at greatest risk from extreme heat placed Nagpur, Chennai, Bengaluru, and 11 other Indian cities in the global top 50 — driven not just by soaring temperatures but by limited infrastructure, aging populations, and socioeconomic vulnerability.
articles.image_caption: Indian cities face compounding heat risks from soaring temperatures and limited cooling infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with aging parents in any of 14 Indian cities ranked among the world's most heat-vulnerable need a concrete plan — from cooling infrastructure to medication reviews — before the next summer peak.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asians Face Higher Heart Risk by 45 Despite Healthier Habits, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A decade-long Northwestern study of 2,700 adults reveals a troubling paradox: South Asians report better diets and lower alcohol use but develop prediabetes and hypertension at double the rate of white Americans by midlife.
articles.image_caption: A blood pressure screening — a major new study finds South Asians face significantly higher cardiovascular risk by age 45 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face uniquely elevated cardiovascular risk that standard BMI and lifestyle metrics fail to capture, demanding earlier screening and culturally tailored health interventions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Bhag Club to Bombay On Foot: How India's Run Club Boom Is Rewriting the Wellness Playbook
articles.excerpt: Across India's cities, running clubs are replacing bar crawls as the new social ritual — and the movement is resonating with the diaspora seeking community beyond the treadmill.
articles.image_caption: Runners gather for an early morning group run in an Indian city park
articles.nri_angle: NRIs watching India's community fitness explosion are finding parallels in their own cities — and many are launching or joining similar run clubs abroad, bridging diaspora loneliness with the Indian ethos of collective wellness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Science Is Settling: What 104 Clinical Trials Say About Turmeric's Real Health Benefits
articles.excerpt: A sweeping meta-analysis of over 100 randomized controlled trials finds that curcumin supplementation significantly lowers blood sugar, cholesterol, and inflammation — but the dose and form matter more than your grandmother's golden milk recipe.
articles.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root and ground curcumin powder, staples of South Asian kitchens
articles.nri_angle: For South Asians who grew up with turmeric as kitchen medicine, the largest-ever clinical review validates what their grandmothers always said — while revealing that traditional culinary doses and modern supplements are not the same thing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
